correctness.rationale: For every connected simple G with an edge, bipartite parity and shared endpoints give the complete radius-two metric adjacency taxonomy. Pairwise intersecting edges form a star or a three-edge triangle, so every simplex belongs to Cl(G), a vertex-star simplex, an edge triangle, or an exceptional midpoint triangle. In the core excluding only the latter triangles, decreasing-cardinality star pairs are genuine elementary free-face collapses and edge triangle/edge pairs remove all midpoints, leaving Cl(G). Each exceptional triangle boundary is homotopic in the core to its original filled graph triangle and hence nullhomotopic, proving the unrestricted wedge decomposition by the CW attaching lemma. The induced H1 map equals the quotient by triangular graph cycles. The standalone verifier checked the entire 1099-graph census up to five vertices, six larger named instances, elementary freeness, complete face coverage and independent mod-two homology. Finite checks are corroboration, not the basis of the quantified proof.

originality.rationale: Direct comparison with the closest published exact-object result shows it classifies only S(K_n), whose Cl(K_n) is a simplex. The arbitrary-base-graph homotopy component, all-triangles decomposition and integral first-persistence map are not implied by that special case. Searches across graph square/edge subdivision/incidence/Rips/triangle aliases and material inspection of relevant Rips and metric-gluing literature found no covering theorem. This is best-knowledge originality, not proof of uniqueness; unindexed or renamed exact equivalences remain possible.

value.rationale: This supplies a structural, exact integral homotopy reduction for every finite connected graph, rather than a numerical invariant on an arbitrary narrow example. Every connected finite flag complex is Cl(G) for some finite connected graph G, so complicated fundamental groups and higher-dimensional/torsion phenomena may persist unchanged through subdivision Rips thickening while each base triangle contributes exactly one free S². The first integral persistent H1 map is explicitly identified as the quotient by triangular cycles. The arbitrary-core theorem is not a routine restatement of complete-graph computations and supports future investigations of topology under graph-subdivision transformations.
